name: Adobe Acrobat Reader
summary: Free Adobe Acrobat Reader desktop Classic/perpetual release lines; excludes paid Adobe Acrobat (Pro/Standard), which is a separate product, and the subscription Continuous track

evidence.quote: As stated in the Adobe Support Lifecycle Policy , Adobe provides five years of product support, starting from the general availability date of Adobe Reader and Adobe Acrobat. In line with this policy, support for Adobe Acrobat 10.x and Adobe Reader 10.x ended on November 15, 2015.

As stated in the Adobe Support Lifecycle Policy , Adobe provides five years of product support, starting from the general availability date of Adobe Reader and Adobe Acrobat. In line with this policy, support for Adobe Acrobat 11.x and Adobe Reader 11.x ends on October 15, 2017.

As stated in the Adobe Support Lifecycle Policy , Adobe provides five years of product support, starting from the general availability date of Adobe Acrobat and Acrobat Reader. In line with this policy, support for Adobe Acrobat 2017 Classic and Acrobat Reader 2017 Classic ends on June 06, 2022.
End of support for Adobe Acrobat 2020 and Acrobat Reader 2020

notes: Tier: researched (AGENTS.md rule 8b). Same reasoning as contributions/adobe-acrobat.json: no deterministic source covers this product (endoflife.date all.json has no acrobat or acrobat-reader slug as of 2026-09-17; no local record). Scope: the free Adobe Acrobat Reader desktop product only; paid Acrobat Pro/Standard is the separate product in contributions/adobe-acrobat.json, and its rows are deliberately absent here, so the two records never conflate the paid and free products even though both cite the same vendor matrix. Full-matrix inventory, not just the A-B section: the whole page was fetched (all A-B through S-Z sections) and every Reader-named row is published above. Reader 7.x, 8.x, 9.x, Reader X, Reader XI, Acrobat Reader 2015 (classic) and Acrobat Reader 2020 are the complete set of Reader rows on the matrix. Reader 2024 has no row anywhere on the page and no notice dates a Reader 2024 Classic, so no such line is asserted. Reader 2017 Classic is the one line the matrix omits while Adobe's own live notice still dates it verbatim (see that evidence quote); because it is an announced retirement with an explicit vendor date, it is published with its end of life 2022-06-06 and ga left null rather than dropped, per AGENTS.md rules 7 and 8b. Its date comes from the notice alone -- no matrix row exists to corroborate it -- which is exactly why the quote is stored beside it. No Reader release ever states an end of extended support: every Reader row carries N/A there, so eos and eossec stay null. Two matrix rows are excluded as different products: Reader Extensions Server (all platforms) 6.1 is a server product, not the desktop Reader, and the LiveCycle Reader Extensions ES/ES2/ES3/ES4 rows are LiveCycle server products. The subscription Continuous (evergreen Document Cloud) Reader track is excluded explicitly: it has no row on the vendor matrix, so it carries no published lifecycle date and none is invented. Where a cell carries an extension (2015: 4/7/2020 extended until 7/7/2020; 2020: 6/1/2025 extended until 11/30/2025) the extended date is stored as the end-of-life date, because it is the last date the vendor states the product is supported; the original core-support date is preserved verbatim in the quote beside it. Every matrix date is mm/dd/yyyy (the page's own note: All dates in mm/dd/yyyy format), so this contribution also needs the contribute.py day matcher to read US M/D/YYYY spellings. Adobe's own 2015 notice (/acrobat/kb/end-of-support-acrobat-2015-reader-2015.html, the page the matrix row itself links) now redirects to the Acrobat desktop hub and no longer states that date, so 2015 is cited to the matrix only.
